To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) muscarinic receptor activation stimulates the synthesis of phosphatidic acid and phosphatidylnositol; (2) this is associated with a decrease in the labeling (and presumably the synthesis) of the polyphosphate derivatives of phosphatidylnsitol; (3) this effect is not due to increased de novo synthesis or increased precursor pool size; (4) the effect of muscarinic agonism on phosphatidic and phosphatidyinositol labeling

the ionophore a23187 and acetylcholine, acting synergistically, stimulate phospholipase C in brain synaptosomes, as evidenced by a selective increase in the labeling of phospholipids containing phosphatidate and phosphatidyinositol, and a decrease in the labeling in phospholipids with phosphoinositides.
ACh or A23I87, alone or in combination, stimulate the labeling of phospholipid by 32Pi.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the biochemical mechanisms underlying cholinergic receptor function.
the mechanism by which A23187 enhances the effects of muscarinic agonist on synaptosomal phosphoinositides.
the mechanism by which ACh and A23l87 alter the incorporation of [32P]-orthophosphate into phospholipids in rat brain synaptic membranes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the activation of phospholipase C is a major component in the mechanism of muscarinic receptor action, and that this enzyme is regulated by the calcium concentration of the synaptosomal cytoplasm.
ACh and A23l87 interact with muscarinic receptors, and that the resultant stimulation of phospholipid metabolism involves both phosphodiesteratic and phosphorylation/dephosphorylation mechanisms.
the muscarinic receptor activation of phosphoinositide turnover is mediated by the mobilization of Ca2+ and that this is a necessary, but not sufficient, requirement for this activation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the muscarinic receptor is linked to a calcium-dependent phospholipid kinase, the product of which is phosphatidylinositide.
ACh and A 23187 synergistically increase the turnover of PhA, PhIP and PhI, and decrease that of the polyphinositides.
the activation of musccarinic receptors by ACh or ionophore results in the activation of phospholipase C and the generation of diglyceride.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the muscarinic agonist-induced increase in the turnover of the phosphoinositide pool is not the result of an increased availability of the precursor, [32P]phosphate, or increased de-novo synthesis of the phosphoinositol lipids, but rather the result of an enhanced rate of cleavage of the phosphodiester bonds of the polyphos-phoinositides.
the ionophore, A23187, enhances the effects of muscarinic agonist on synaptosomal phosphoinositide metabolism.
the muscarinic agonist, ACh, can alter phospholipid metabolism by at least two distinct mechanisms.
